newsitem.title: CANADA: Thiessen sees rising Canada dollar, 4 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: Thiessen sees rising Canada dollar, 4 pct growth.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said on Tuesday that he saw the Canadian dollar appreciating against the U.S. dollar over the long term.
Thiessen also repeated his previous predictions of four percent growth in gross domestic product in 1997, comparing the fourth quarter of 1997 to fourth-quarter 1996.
He said that the Canadian dollar should appreciate with Canada's expected economic growth, an improving balance of payments and a stable political environment, .
"All of these things are going to lead to an upside potential for the Canadian dollar," he said.
I do believe there's an underlying upward trend," he told reporters after addressing the Senate's banking committee.
But Thiessen declined to say to what he thought Canada's natural rate of unemployment was -- the rate of unemployment when the economy was producing at full capacity.
"It's so difficult to say," he said.
Canada's unemployment rate has been stuck around 9.7 percent for months.
Thiessen said the Bank of Canada was studying economic growth in the United States, where there the unemployment rate had edged down while inflation stayed relatively low.
